title: Air-fryer honey garlic wings
subtitle: Sticky sweet-savoury wings glazed with honey and garlic.
excerpt: Chicken wings air-fried until crisp, then tossed in a sticky honey-garlic glaze with a little soy sauce. The glaze caramelises when you return the wings to the fryer for a final two minutes. Serves two as a main or four as a snack.
sourceNotes: Honey-garlic chicken is a popular preparation across North American and East Asian home cooking traditions. The combination of honey, soy sauce, and garlic creates a glaze that caramelises quickly at high heat.

content.text: Honey-garlic wings are a two-stage cook: first cook the wings until crisp, then toss in the glaze and return to the fryer for two minutes to caramelise the surface. Applying the glaze before the initial cook would burn before the meat is done.

Pat {{chicken-wings}} of wings dry. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and spray with cooking oil. Preheat the air fryer to 200°C and cook the wings in a single layer for 12 minutes. Flip and cook for a further 10 minutes until golden and cooked through.

While the wings cook, combine {{honey}} of honey, {{soy-sauce-light}} of light soy sauce, and {{garlic}} of grated garlic in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Toss the cooked wings in the glaze, return them to the air fryer basket, and cook at 200°C for 2 minutes more so the glaze sets and caramelises slightly. Scatter with sesame seeds if using.

items.cause: Final glaze step run too long or temperature too high.
items.fix: The glaze step is only 2 minutes at 200°C. Watch it closely ,  honey burns quickly past the caramelisation point.

items.symptom: Glaze too thin and runs off
items.cause: Glaze not reduced enough before tossing.
items.fix: Simmer the glaze until it coats the back of a spoon before tossing the wings.

items.symptom: Wings not crisp under the glaze
items.cause: Wings not cooked through properly before glazing.
items.fix: The first cook should give you properly crisp wings. Glaze goes on at the end, not before.

content.text: Honey-garlic wings sit between a snack and a light meal. Good with steamed rice, or piled on a plate alongside chips. The glaze also works on chicken thighs ,  cook for longer at the same temperature and glaze in the final five minutes.
